“The reducible held out loss (R-HOL) is an information-theoretic loss selection function which chooses points that are just right for training, and it trains faster than other loss selection functions.” The main contribution of our work is the R-HOL function, which is a novel loss selection function for training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of training a model on a finite set of training examples.
how we can train a model to learn more efficiently and effectively.
the problem of selecting training points that are both learnable and worth learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RHOLS is a technique for faster training that selects a sequence of just right training points, that are worth learning and not yet learned.
RHOLS is an effective and efficient technique for faster model optimization and training.
our method outperforms other state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin on all of the datasets we tested on.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method to select a sequence of training samples to maximize the information of the heldout loss.
the proposed method, RHOLS, is a general technique to improve training speed for any supervised learning model.
we propose a novel acquisition function, RHOLS, that selects a training sequence which is optimal for the held-out set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model can learn faster if it is given a sequence of training samples which are “just right”.
the choice of which training points to use is as important as the choice of how to use them.
the best points to train on are those that are worth learning, not yet learned, and are learnable.
